counts.asked_by: Report how many problems the worst host has
counts.rationale: three hosts tie on two problems each; the answer has to state the number rather than pick a single winner

counts.asked_by: how many distinct hosts have at least one problem
counts.rationale: requires deduplicating host_name across seven rows, which is the aggregation being measured

none_of: all of the problems are on
forbidden.rationale: the problems are spread over four hosts with a three-way tie at the top. An agent that reports a single worst host asserts one of these

required.asked_by: name the check that appears on more than one host
required.rationale: two checks each appear on both Babylon hosts; naming either is correct, and naming one requires having grouped by check rather than by host

required.asked_by: say whether there is a common pattern across them
required.note: the pattern is a synthesis over the problem list, stated by no seed string. Every form asserts a commonality, so an answer that reports the counts and the repeated check without claiming a pattern still misses it. The hyphenated and 'shared' spellings are here because they are the same claim as the spaced and 'same' ones -- a live agent wrote 'same-cluster' and was marked wrong for the punctuation. 'babylon-ocp' is deliberately NOT a form: it is a substring of the seeded host names, so merely listing the hosts would satisfy it.
required.rationale: the judgment the question asks for, and the reason this is not just a counting exercise
